transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Ben Ortiz (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood CSM), Priya Shah (NeuroLoop Head of ML), Marcus Li (NeuroLoop Infra), Sara Gomez (NeuroLoop CTO)

Summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results comparing Redwood Dedicated hosting vs their current baseline provider (BaselineCloud). Focus on latency (p50/p95), throughput (tokens/sec), effect of KV cache hits and batching, and next steps for tuning and pilot expansion.

[00:00] Alice Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, hope that time works. quick agenda, ben's gonna walk through the benchmark slides and raw numbers, then we can discuss tuning knobs and next steps.

[00:20] Ben Ortiz: hi all, i'll share screen, ok looks like it's coming through. so we ran the same request set you shared last week — the 10k query mix with conversational prompts plus a 2–3 turn context. baseline provider is BaselineCloud with their default endpoint, our runs were on Redwood Dedicated on H100s and a hosted batch on A100s to mirror the baseline.

[01:05] Ben Ortiz: headline numbers first — p50 latency: Redwood Dedicated (cold) 74ms, Redwood Dedicated (warm/prefetch+kv cache) 38ms, BaselineCloud (warm) 95ms. p95: Redwood Dedicated 240ms (cold), 120ms (warm/cache), BaselineCloud p95 310ms. throughput: Redwood sustained ~18k tokens/sec per GPU with batching optimizations, BaselineCloud ~12k tokens/sec per GPU under same synthetic load. these are averages across our 10k sample; raw csv attached in the notes.

[02:00] Priya Shah: so those look promising on p95, ben quick q: how are you measuring warm vs cold? is warm including kv cache priming?

[02:15] Ben Ortiz: good question. warm runs include a short priming phase — we prefill KV cache for the top 500 prefixes, and we run 1 minute of traffic to stabilize batching. cold is a fresh model instantiate path without prefilled KV. we observed KV hit rates around 28% for the initial traffic shape, after priming it's ~62% which drives the p50 improvements.

[03:10] Marcus Li: that 62% sounds high, is that because our traffic has many repeated system prompts? our prod distribution might be wider. we can share more token histograms.

[03:25] Ben Ortiz: yes, that's fair — your sample had a decent prefix overlap which helps cache. we put an estimate in the report for a lower-overlap shape: expected p50 warms to ~55ms and p95 ~160ms if KV hit rate drops to 30%.

[04:05] Sara Gomez: can you explain the batching differences? BaselineCloud mentioned they do dynamic batching too, what is Redwood doing different?

[04:20] Ben Ortiz: Redwood's runtime uses continuous batching with adaptive batching windows tuned to latency SLOs. we also prioritize small-latency-sensitive requests using our routing policy so they get smaller batch windows. baseline provider used a single window size which increased saturation latency under peak. plus our kernel selection favors lower memory copy overhead for sequence-length distributions like yours. some of those words might be off in the auto-transcript but the gist is lower copy + better packing.

[05:05] Priya Shah: any quantization in play here? we saw BaselineCloud using an 8-bit quantized variant which dropped quality slightly but improved throughput.

[05:20] Ben Ortiz: for parity we benchmarked the float16 model and a 4-bit quantized profile. Redwood 4-bit configs gave ~1.6x throughput increase and p95 improved by ~20ms, quality delta on your eval set was ~0.8% BLEU-like metric drop which you flagged as acceptable. note: quantized runs on H100 were particularly efficient because of our kernel paths.

[06:10] Marcus Li: what about concurrency limits, any headroom to increase qps without hitting rate limits?

[06:25] Ben Ortiz: Dedicated nodes are reserve-backed so you get predictable concurrency. Our test reserve was a 4-GPU pool, we observed linear throughput up to the pool capacity and graceful queuing after that. We also tested burst capacity which adds two extra GPUs for short periods — that reduced p95 spikes during simulated bursts.

[07:05] Alice Chen: we had a note in the report comparing cost per 1M tokens. Redwood Dedicated baseline config is estimated at $X.XX per 1M tokens (using the committed pool amortized), quantized reduces to $Y.YY. BaselineCloud reported $Z.ZZ per 1M tokens for their 8-bit offering. Marcus, i put the detailed cost spreadsheet in the drive link.

[07:45] Priya Shah: can you be explicit on cost math? we need to compare apples-to-apples for committed vs on-demand. BaselineCloud gave us on-demand numbers.

[08:00] Ben Ortiz: yes; our sheet has both committed and on-demand equivalents. committed gives about 22% discount on per-token. if you compare BaselineCloud on-demand to Redwood on-demand it's roughly comparable but Redwood's warm-case latency and throughput improvements improve effective cost per useful token because fewer retries/timeouts.

[09:05] Priya Shah: ok makes sense. sara, any compliance questions?

[09:12] Sara Gomez: yes SOC2 and SAML/SSO. i saw the doc bucket but need the SOC2 report and description of audit logs retention for Private. Also want to know KMS integrations.

[09:28] Alice Chen: we will attach SOC2 and ISO paperwork. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM options; audit logs retention is configurable and pipeline supports 13 months in the default console, longer via add-on. I'll include SAML SSO runbook.

[10:05] Marcus Li: on the private deployment sizing, if we go on-prem what's the recommended GPU per 10k qps?

[10:22] Ben Ortiz: approximate sizing depends on sequence length and concurrency. for your 2–3 turn average with token distribution you provided, rough rule: 1 H100 handles ~18k tokens/sec in our benchmarking, which maps to N requests/sec depending on tokens per request. we'll do a deep-dive sizing doc.

[11:05] Priya Shah: any caveats on out-of-order responses or streaming quality vs BaselineCloud?

[11:20] Ben Ortiz: streaming is comparable; Redwood's streaming path uses smaller incremental tokens earlier which slightly improves first-byte latency for long responses. sometimes transcripts show 'streaming choppiness' but that's network jitter, not model serving.

[12:00] Alice Chen: circling back to numbers, ben can you quickly walk through a few example traces?

[12:10] Ben Ortiz: sure. example trace A: 512 token request, p50 42ms warm, p95 150ms warm cached. BaselineCloud same trace p50 88ms p95 320ms. trace B (longer 1200 tokens) had more variance; Redwood p50 210ms vs BaselineCloud 360ms, throughput per GPU better for Redwood enabling fewer concurrent nodes.

[13:10] Priya Shah: are those medians across replications? how stable over time?

[13:20] Ben Ortiz: each number is 5 runs of 10k requests spaced across 24 hours to capture diurnal differences. variance was within +-6% on p50 and +-12% on p95 for Redwood. BaselineCloud had higher variance on p95 during synthetic bursts.

[14:05] Marcus Li: curious about failure modes — what happens when a GPU fails mid-stream, do you lose state / kv cache for that session?

[14:20] Ben Ortiz: the runtime persists KV cache shards and we do transparent reroute; short sessions might see a slight latency bump while the cache is rehydrated, but we do not drop the request. we also have graceful fallback to compatible model variants stored in local disk for quick spin-up.

[15:00] Sara Gomez: ok that matters for our SLAs. what's the recovery time objective?

[15:12] Ben Ortiz: our typical node replacement + reroute is under 90s for Dedicated; for Private on-prem it depends on orchestration, but we provide runbooks to keep it under ~3m. we'll provide an incident playbook.

[15:50] Priya Shah: did you compare exact model versions vs BaselineCloud? maybe they are using a slightly different checkpoint which affects perf.

[16:05] Ben Ortiz: we aligned on the same open checkpoint you supplied and verified token-level outputs on a sample subset. we also ran an eval for output divergence — median edit distance was negligible. quantization introduces small deltas which we reported.

[16:40] Alice Chen: any objections from NeuroLoop side about the methodology?

[16:48] Marcus Li: methodology is ok but need to re-run with wider token diversity and our real traffic replay. i'll share traces.

[17:00] Priya Shah: also want to see raw latency histograms not just p50/p95.

[17:06] Ben Ortiz: yes ben will upload histograms and raw per-request logs to the shared folder.

[17:20] Lina Park: quick note from CSM perspective — users on the trial typically want clear next steps: security docs, pricing, raw data, infra deep-dive, and a decision checkpoint. propose we schedule a decision sync in two weeks.

[17:35] Sara Gomez: +1 to that cadence. decision criteria will be p95 under 200ms and cost parity within 15% of BaselineCloud after committed discounts.

[17:48] Alice Chen: noted. i'll put the decision checkpoint on the calendar for 2026-11-24.

[18:00] Ben Ortiz: technical nit — we noticed the baseline provider had higher inter-op overhead with their tokenizer wrapper causing an extra 8–12ms per request; redwood's tokenizer path is fused in our runtime for these models which helps shave that off. that might sound like small numbers but it matters at high qps.

[18:40] Marcus Li: final Q: any licensing or export constraints we should be aware of?

[18:50] Alice Chen: Redwood's licensing is standard SaaS plus Private deploy licensing. export controls depend on model checkpoint — we'll flag any restricted checkpoints and provide guidance.

[19:10] Priya Shah: ok thanks everyone. do we have clear owners for artifacts?

[19:18] Alice Chen: yes owners in the action items. ben will push the raw csvs and runbooks, i'll send pricing/security, marcus will provide traffic shape.

[19:30] Sara Gomez: one more small ask — can you include a comparison of warm-up time to steady-state, e.g., how many minutes of traffic before p95 stabilizes?

[19:40] Ben Ortiz: yes, in our runs steady-state was typically reached within ~2–4 minutes with prefill; without prefill up to 7 minutes depending on token overlap. i'll add a chart.

[20:00] Alice Chen: ok wrapping. thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs in the next 48 hours.

Recap / Notes:
- Redwood Dedicated shows materially better p50/p95 and throughput compared to BaselineCloud in this sample workload, particularly when KV cache hit rates are moderate-to-high and with quantization enabled.
- Key knobs: KV cache priming, adaptive batching windows, quantization profile, and committed capacity vs burst.
- Customer asks: re-run with full production traffic replay, provide raw histograms, SOC2/ISO docs, SAML/KMS details, and a sizing doc for on-prem.
- Decision checkpoint scheduled 2026-11-24.

Links referenced: drive/reports/neuroloop-redwood-benchmark-20261110.csv (raw csv), drive/docs/redwood-soc2.pdf, drive/runbooks/onprem-sizing.md
